div.fw: A Sergeaıı̄unt of Lawe \ A Francleyn̄
div.l: Of hem that fonde hym wherewith to scole ay
Of study toke he most cure and kepe
Nought oo word spake he more þan̄ was nede
And þat was seyd in forme and reủerens
And schorte and qwykke and full high of senten̄s
Sownynge in morall vertu was his speche
And gladely wold he lerne and gladly teche
¶ A Sergeaunt of lawe also war͗ and wyse
That often̄ tyme had ben̄ at parvys
That was also full of excellense
Dyscrete he was and of gret Reủerens
He semed such his wordes were so wyse
Iustyse he was full ofte in assyse
By patent and by comyssyoıı̄un
For his scyens and for his hiȝe renoun̄
Off fees and Robes had he many one
So grete a purchaser nas nowher͗ none
All was fee sympull to hȳm in effecte
His purchasynge myȝte nouȝte ben infecte
Nowhere so Byssy a man̄ as he þ̉er nas
And yette he semed bysyer þan̄ he was
In termes had he caas and domes alle ·
That fro the tyme of kynge Willam wer͗ falle
Therto he kowde endyte and make a thynge
There kowde no wyght pynche at his wrytyng
And eủery statute kowde he pleyn̄ by Rote
He rode but homely in A medle cote
Gyrde with a seynte of sylke with barrꝰus smale
Of his Aray tell y no leng̉er tale
¶ A Francleyn̄ was in þat company
